blocks.text: Dear Ms. Alvarez:

You gave us the better part of an afternoon last week, and most of it went to what this role is for and very little of it to what it costs. That order helps us more than you might think. We would be glad to conduct the search. This letter sets out the agreement between us, and I have written it in plain language so that it can be read once and understood.
Please read it against your own notes from that afternoon. If a term here sits differently from what you understood, telephone me before you sign and we will settle it between us.
The Role We Are Retained to Fill

Northgate will conduct a retained search for the general counsel of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}, reporting to you. The role is defined by a written position specification. We draft it with you, you approve it, and no one is approached before you have. Everything after that point is measured against it. If the market disagrees with the specification, and on a role of this kind the market usually has an opinion, we bring the disagreement back to you and change the document openly.

Two things sit outside this letter. We are not reviewing your outside counsel arrangements, and we are not searching for the other positions we touched on at the end of the afternoon. Either can be taken up under a separate engagement. If this search raises a question of that kind, and searches for a first senior lawyer often do, we will put it in front of you and wait for your instruction before we act on it.
Our Method, Stage by Stage
The work runs in five stages and each one gates the next. You will know at any point in the search which stage we are in and what is holding up the one after it.

items: 1. Specification. We interview you and the executives this lawyer will sit alongside, then draft a document that states what the role owns, what it does not, and what a person must have done before to hold it. Your approval closes the stage.

2. Market map. We chart where lawyers of this description actually sit today: your revenue band, the two sectors either side of it, and the firms that serve them. You see the map, so that you can tell us where we have looked in the wrong place.
3. Approach. Our consultants make every approach themselves and by telephone. Nothing goes out until you have read the long list with us and told us where you disagree with it.
4. Assessment. Everyone carried forward is interviewed against the specification and written up before they travel any further. Nobody reaches a slate on the strength of a good conversation alone.

5. Slate and references. We present the slate in person, take the references on the finalists ourselves, and stay with you through the offer and through the resignation your candidate has to go and hand in.

blocks.text: We are retained rather than contingent, and the difference shows up in how we behave rather than in what we charge. What you are buying is the whole of the market looked at properly, including the parts of it that turn out to hold no one, and an honest account of what we found there.
Who Will Do the Work

Sandra Fuentes leads the search and is your point of contact from the first specification interview through to the day the appointment is announced. James Grant works the assessment alongside her and takes the second read on every candidate who reaches a written appraisal. Nicole Donovan holds the research, the record, and the calendar; when you need a session moved or a document sent, she is the shortest route to it. I remain accountable for the engagement. If at any point you are not getting what this letter describes, telephone me directly and say so.

One habit of ours is worth stating now, because it will show up in every document you receive from us. Candidates are described by the role they hold today and the scale of the business they hold it in, never by name, until they have spoken to their own employer and are ready for the conversation to be real. In a market this size, one name in the wrong room ends a search and does a good deal of damage on its way out.
Fee, Expenses, and When Work Begins

Our fee for this search is a fixed {{fact:f:E-2019-001.fee}}, payable in three parts: one third on your signature of this letter, one third when we present the slate, and the balance when your chosen candidate accepts. The fee does not move with the salary you agree, and we take no percentage of it. Invoices fall due thirty days from issue.

Expenses are billed at cost and itemized on each invoice: our travel to interviews, candidate travel where we have asked someone to come to you, and any external verification you instruct us to run. We ask your approval in advance for any item of real consequence. Our work begins {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}, and the specification interviews are the first thing we will want in the diary.
How Long This Runs, and How It Ends

We plan the search over about four months from the day work begins. Searches move at the speed of the calendars involved, and if we come to think we are behind we will tell you at that moment and not at the point where it has become obvious to both of us. Either of us may end this engagement on thirty days' written notice. If you end it, you owe the portion of the fee earned to that date together with expenses already incurred, and we hand over the specification, the market map, and the record of every conversation held on your behalf. Nothing in the file is kept back.
What Stays Between Us

What you tell us about {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}, about your people, and about your plans stays inside the engagement team and is never carried into another search. The same protection runs the other way for the candidates we speak to, which is why their names reach you and go no further. For the term of this engagement and for twelve months after it closes, we will not approach an employee of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} on behalf of another client of this firm.
The Limits of What We Promise

We do not guarantee an appointment. We guarantee the work: the market covered, every candidate assessed against the specification you approved, and a straight account of what we found, including the parts you would have preferred we had not. Our liability under this agreement is limited to the fees you have paid us under it. If the lawyer we place leaves within twelve months, other than through redundancy or a material change to the role, we conduct one replacement search and charge you expenses only.
The Law That Applies

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office is established, and any dispute arising under it belongs in the courts of that state. If a provision of this letter is found unenforceable, the remainder stands. Signed, this letter is the whole of the agreement between us on this search, and neither of us should rely on anything said before it.

If this reflects your understanding, please sign both copies and return one to me. The next step is a short one. Sandra Fuentes will telephone your office this week to fix the specification interviews for the opening days of the engagement, and we would ask that the second of them include whoever manages your work with outside counsel today.

To: Sandra Fuentes, James Grant
From: Nicole Donovan
Re: General counsel search for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}, opening plan and division of work
Copy: engagement file

The engagement opened {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}} and this memo is the record of what we settled in the room afterwards. Amy Alvarez is our client on the assignment and the role reports to her. Everything below is what I will hold the file to until one of you tells me to change it.
The objective, stated once

Present a slate of general counsel candidates who can carry the legal work of a business this size without a department behind them. The work going to outside firms today is commercial contracts and employment, and the client wants that judgment inside the business and available in the week it is asked for rather than in the week after.

Two constraints from the intake session shape the map and are worth repeating. Amy Alvarez wants a lawyer who has been the only one in a room of operators and was comfortable there. She also said, without being asked, that a candidate whose first move is to build a team is not the candidate.
Who owns which piece
Five pieces, in the order each one unlocks the next. I have put the owner on every line so that nobody has to come and ask me in three weeks.

items: 1. Specification. Sandra Fuentes runs both sessions at the client and drafts from them. I sit in and keep the record. No part of it reaches a candidate before Amy Alvarez has approved the draft in writing.

2. Market map. Mine to build: businesses in the client's revenue band and the two sectors either side of it, and the counsel, deputy counsel, and head of legal titles sitting inside them. I am building it to be defensible rather than long.
3. Long list. Mine to draw off the map and not off our files. James Grant reads it before a single name is approached, and Sandra Fuentes takes it to the client.
4. Approach wording. James Grant owns it. Every approach goes by telephone and by a consultant, and I log who was approached, when, by what route, and what came back.
5. Reporting. A written update to Amy Alvarez every fortnight and a working session at each review point. Sandra Fuentes holds the client relationship. I draft, she signs.

blocks.text: Unsettled, and it changes the approach

Two questions are open and both belong in the first specification session. We do not know whether the role carries the compliance work as well as the contracts, and lawyers at this level ask early because the answer decides how much of their week is their own. We also do not know what the client wants said if a candidate's employer hears about the search, which on a search of this kind is a live possibility.
Neither question belongs in an email. I have put both at the top of the agenda for the first session so that they are answered while everyone with a view is in the room.
Before the first session

Scheduling gates everything else, so it is the first job and it is mine. I will ask Amy Alvarez today for two blocks inside the next fortnight, and I will hold slots that work for James Grant as well, since he should hear the brief first hand instead of reading my notes of it.
Sandra Fuentes, the outline for the specification is yours. My intake notes are in the engagement file and they are a good deal fuller than the summary I circulated after the session.

James Grant, I need your read on the approach wording before I make any research calls. Nothing goes into the market until it is settled. If you would rather the first draft came from me, say so and I will write it against the intake notes and send it up.
Hi Amy,

The specification is signed off and the market work behind it is finished, so the next thing on the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} general counsel search is the long list session with you. I am starting this thread to keep the updates in one place, and Sandra and James are on copy throughout.

Where the work stands. The map covers your revenue band and the two sectors either side of it, and it closed at thirty-eight people of the right seniority. Nineteen of those are worth a first conversation on what we can see of them from the outside. Nobody has been approached, and nobody will be until you have read the list with Sandra.

There are two things I need from you before any approach goes out. One is ninety minutes inside the next fortnight for the list session, at your office or ours, and I will build it around whatever windows you can give me. The other is your ruling on which companies are off limits to us. Your outside counsel firms are the obvious ones; any business where a call from us would be awkward for you belongs on that list too, and I would rather have the awkward names than guess at them.
Send me the windows and I will confirm the session today.
Regards
Hi Amy,
The list you read at that session will hold fewer sitting general counsel than the specification implies, and you should hear why from me before it is in front of you.

The specification asks for a lawyer who already holds the title inside a business the size of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} and who knows your regulatory ground. Both of those are reasonable on their own, and the place where they overlap is thin. The people who sit squarely in it are mostly not moving this year. The deeper field is deputies and heads of legal doing the same work under somebody else's title, and the good ones are ready for the step.

I am not asking you to lower the bar, and I would not recommend it. I am asking you to tell us, before the approaches start, which of the two you would keep if you could only keep one, because that answer decides who we call first. Bring it to the session and the list we walk you through will be honest about the trade.

The research carries on while you think about it. The calls we are making this week are the ones that tell us how thin the overlap really is, and I will have a better answer for you by the session than I have this morning.
Best regards
Hi Amy,
That is enough to work with, thank you, and the session is held.

The four companies you named are marked off limits in the engagement file and nobody here will put a call into any of them without your say. I have logged your reason against each one so the file explains itself to whoever reads it later.

I have taken the second of the two windows you offered and the invitation is with your assistant. Sandra and James both come. Two things would help before it: the names and titles of whoever will sit in the interviews, and whatever you have in writing on how the outside counsel work runs today, since the list reads better against a picture of what this person is actually inheriting. If the panel is not settled yet, send me who you expect it to be and I will correct the file later.

The list itself reaches you the day before, by courier and not by email, and it describes people by the role they hold now. That is how we work on every search, not a precaution we have invented for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}.
Regards
Hi Amy,

Yes, and it is the right question to have asked. A deputy who has run the contract work for a business twice your size is often the stronger appointment, and two of the people I most want you to see are in exactly that position today.

What that means for the session is small. When you read the list, the line that matters is what the person owns now, not the title on the card, and we will lay it out that way so the comparison is a fair one. I will say a sentence about each of them before you read anything.

On your point about timing, the approaches go out in the week after we have read the list together, and the first conversations are deliberately informal; nobody is negotiating with anybody at that stage, {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} is not named until a candidate has shown real interest, and no candidate's name leaves our file until they know their own mind, which is usually two conversations in.
If anything else has occurred to you, send it before Monday and I will fold it into the agenda.
Best regards
